svg.title: The fat-header threshold
svg.desc: Annotated byte axis of the fat-header probe over one TLS session. Gates at 8 KiB (late_stage_cutoff once a response is seen), 14 KiB (fat_threshold_reached, 16384 minus 2048 bytes), and 16 KiB (FAT_HEADER_THRESHOLD_BYTES). A cut-off at the threshold is logged tcp_16kb_blocked, the focal signal. Below, classify_rst_origin splits a reset by timing: in_path_rst within twice the SYN-ACK RTT, server_rst later.
svg.text: BYTES SENT · ONE TLS SESSION · FAT_HEADER_REQUESTS = 16
The probe records the byte offset of the break, not a bare reset — the position on the axis is the evidence.
The 2× RTT rule charges the reset to the in-path box when it arrives too fast to have come from the remote server.
